basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ADOPTING THE OFFICIAL FLAG OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Adopts the official flag of the Bangsamoro — green, white and red bands with a golden crescent and seven-rayed star, and a white kris — and requires government offices and schools across the region to fly it.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The Organic Law (RA 11054), Article II Section 2, allows the region to adopt its own flag as part of its right to self-governance. This act exercises that right and fixes the design so it cannot drift.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The region has one official flag with an exact specification — dimensions, hex colours and proportions — and every Bangsamoro office, public office, school, college, university and government corporation is required to display it, alongside the Philippine flag.
who_will_be_affected: All Bangsamoro government offices, including those outside the area of autonomy
Public offices, government-owned or controlled corporations and other government instrumentalities
Public and private schools, colleges and universities in the region
Anyone producing or reproducing the flag, who now has an exact specification to follow
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2019 — 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The Bangsamoro has an official flag with an exact design, and schools and government offices are required to fly it next to the Philippine flag.
in_practice: Three horizontal bands, each one third: green #009966 on top, white #FFFFFF in the middle, red #FF3333 at the bottom
A golden #FFD700 crescent and seven-rayed star centred on the white band
A white kris on the red band, running 60% of the flag's length
The Philippine flag must always be displayed alongside it

for_specific_groups.Schools: Public and private schools, colleges and universities in the region are required to use and display the flag.
for_specific_groups.Government offices: All Bangsamoro offices, public offices, GOCCs and other instrumentalities must display it — including Bangsamoro offices located outside the region.
for_specific_groups.Flag makers and printers: The act gives exact hex codes and proportions, so a reproduction can be checked against the law.
for_specific_groups.Everyone else: No duty falls on private individuals or businesses.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The BARMM, and Bangsamoro offices outside it.
what_you_can_do: Use the exact colours if you reproduce the flag: green #009966, white #FFFFFF, red #FF3333, gold #FFD700
Expect to see it flown at your school and at government offices, beside the Philippine flag
watch_out_for: The act creates no penalty for failing to display the flag, or for misusing it — the duty is stated without a sanction.
It sets no rules on desecration, half-masting, or the order of precedence beyond requiring the Philippine flag alongside.

key_terms_explained.Kris: The wavy-bladed sword of the region, here a symbol of protection and resistance against oppression, tyranny and injustice.
key_terms_explained.Sakina: Tranquility — the meaning the act gives the white band, along with peace and righteousness.
key_terms_explained.Mujahideen: Those who fought for the recognition of Bangsamoro identity and self-determination; the red band signifies their blood.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 23 August 2019, approved by the Chief Minister on 28 August 2019.

benefits.headline: A single official flag, specified precisely enough that every copy matches.

direct_benefits.benefit: An exact, published design anyone can reproduce correctly
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 3 gives dimensions, hex codes and proportions

indirect_benefits: A shared symbol of regional identity
Recognition in law of the region's history and of those who died in the struggle
limitations: No funding is appropriated for flags.
No penalty attaches to non-display or misuse.

for_government_and_schools: Use and display the Bangsamoro Flag
Always display the Philippine flag alongside it
for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on private individuals.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences — it does not legislate on desecration or misuse.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: The display duty on offices and schools carries no stated sanction.

where_to_complain.note: The act names no implementing body and creates no complaints procedure.

everyday_scenarios: A school principal in Sulu orders new flags. Section 3 gives the exact hex codes and the 3-by-5½-foot size, so the order can be specified against the law rather than by eye.
A barangay office wants to display the Bangsamoro flag alone. The act requires the Philippine flag alongside it.
A shop sells small souvenir flags. The act expressly allows reproduction in small sizes for ceremonial and symbolic purposes.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Adopts an Official Flag of the BARMM pursuant to Article II, Section 2 of the Organic Law (RA 11054).
Section 2 — Policy: in exercising its right to self-governance the region is free to adopt a flag reflective of its peoples' identity, history, heritage, struggles and aspiration.

Section 3 — Design: a standard flag 3 feet by 5½ feet in four colours, carrying a crescent, a seven-rayed star and a kris. The top third is green (#009966) for the Islamic teachings and principles the majority subscribe to; the middle third white (#FFFFFF) for peace, sakina and righteousness; the bottom third red (#FF3333) for the blood of the fallen mujahideen who fought for recognition of identity and self-determination.

Section 3(d) — The crescent and seven-rayed star sit on the white band in golden yellow (#FFD700) for the bright future ahead. The crescent stands for the principles that guided the struggle; the star's seven rays stand for the seven constituent units — Maguindanao, Lanao del Sur with Marawi City, Basilan with Lamitan City, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, the City of Cotabato, and the 63 barangays formerly of North Cotabato.

Section 3(e) — A white kris (#FFFFFF) sits at the centre of the red band, 60% of the flag's length, symbolising the protection and resistance of the Bangsamoro and other indigenous peoples against oppression, tyranny and injustice.

Section 4 — The flag is to be regarded with utmost respect. The Philippine flag must always be displayed alongside it. All Bangsamoro offices, public and private schools, colleges and universities, public offices, government-owned or controlled corporations and other instrumentalities are required to use and display it, including Bangsamoro offices outside the area of autonomy. It may be used ceremonially and reproduced in small sizes.
Section 5 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.a: Green for the Islamic teachings and principles most of the population subscribe to; white for peace, sakina (tranquility) and righteousness; red for the blood of the fallen mujahideen who fought for recognition of Bangsamoro identity and self-determination.

citizen_questions.q: Why seven rays on the star?
citizen_questions.a: One for each constituent unit of the Bangsamoro territory: Maguindanao, Lanao del Sur with Marawi City, Basilan with Lamitan City, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, the City of Cotabato, and the 63 barangays formerly part of North Cotabato.

citizen_questions.q: Do I have to fly it?
citizen_questions.a: Not as a private person. The duty falls on Bangsamoro offices, public offices, government corporations and instrumentalities, and on public and private schools, colleges and universities.

citizen_questions.q: Can it be flown on its own?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 4 requires the Philippine flag always to be displayed alongside it.
Green #009966, white #FFFFFF, red #FF3333, and golden yellow #FFD700 for the crescent and star. The flag is 3 feet by 5½ feet and the kris runs 60% of its length.
